jobs.title: Seventy-two hours
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Thursday. The decision. 'One week. A scorched-earth parody.' The strip draws the sprint's clock: 72 hours as a circle he draws on the wall and starts crossing off. Barnaby goes to sleep for the duration. Panel 1: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a man drawing a clock face with a marker on a garage wall and writing a number in it, a small dog watching, monitor glow (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says "One week. One. A scorched-earth parody of every idiot on that board. Then back to the ridge.". Panel 2: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, close-up of a hand drawing a deliberately crude stick figure with a four-line helicopter rotor on its head on bristol board, the hand tense (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, six crude stick figures at the back of a garage all turning around at once to look at a drawing of a stick figure with a rotor. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a small dog going to sleep in a bed with one eye on a marker clock on the wall that now reads 71, a man drawing at a table in monitor light, no words (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chorus_and_meme is a finished strip in this style. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chorus_and_meme for the character; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
